text:
maya: Noticing a weird p95 -> p99 divergence on the latency dashboard for /v1/generate in eu-prod after the spillover routing change at 11:10. p50 unchanged, p95 +25ms, p99 +120ms. :eyes:
liam: same here. spike only in small requests (seq_len < 32). payloads with longer sequences look normal.
anika: timeline: spillover policy 'overflow-to-fallback' ramped from 0% -> 30% at 11:12 (canary). deploy-bot: Canary canary-2026-03-23T11:10 rolled to 30% at 11:12.
maya: i pulled the dashboard timeseries; the blended line that shows "all-variants" is what jumped. individual variant series show rdw-gpt-q3 has stable tail, rdw-gpt-q4_batched shows the tail.
samir: this smells like tdigest merge weighting with differing sample counts per variant. if we merge sketches without scaling by count, a variant with extreme tail but low count can unduly influence blended p99.
liam: quick check: raw counts in that window -> q4_batched: 420 samples, q3: 4800 samples. but tdigest metadata on the rollups shows both sketches merged without count normalization.
maya: oh interesting. so the blended p99 is being computed by merging two sketches as if equal-population? that will inflate p99 toward the smaller sketch tail.
anika: console-ux can we flag series provenance as "merged_sketches(unweighted)" vs "raw-samples"? people keep assuming blended numbers are sample-weighted.
console-ux: yes. creating a small UX tweak: add a provenance pill and sample-count on hover. quick patch targeted for tomorrow.
liam: for immediate triage i'm running this query to export raw latencies: ```curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "https://telemetry.internal/api/raw?from=6172223000&to=6172223600&route=/v1/generate&env=eu-prod" > /tmp/raw-lats.ndjson```
liam: also checking worker queue metrics: ```/metrics?name=worker_queue_depth&pool=fallback-eu&from=6172223000&to=6172223600```
infra-bot: autoscaler: fallback-eu pool scaled from 6 -> 6 (no scale) at 11:15. average queue depth 7.2 at peak.
maya: queue depth 7.2 with small batch sizes could increase per-request latency if batching waits for fill. batched kernel might wait for batch window, causing tail for small requests.
samir: two hypotheses: 1) tdigest merge bug (unweighted) causing blinded p99; 2) queueing in fallback pool + batching latency. both could be true.
anika: short term dashboard change: split the "all-variants" rollup into two lines: "strict-routing" and "spillover-routing" so we avoid mixing routing policies. console-ux ok?
console-ux: can do. will push a temporary filter and note on the dashboard about blended pctl caveat.
liam: operational mitigation: reduce spillover weight to 5% and monitor. i'll put a rollback plan in the canary thread.
maya: agreed. please also annotate the dashboard with the canary timeline so we don't chase unrelated noise later.
samir: opened telemetry PR #784 to change tdigest merge to preserve sample counts (weighted merge) and to show merged_count in metadata. reviewers: @liam @anika.
liam: reviewing now. small change, but needs unit test for unequal-count merge.
anika: adding a short blurb to the rollout runbook about "percentile blending” and when to prefer raw-sample inspection.
maya: filing incident INC-1240 (pctl: blended p99 surprise during spillover canary). tagging @eng-oncall.
ops-bot: @eng-oncall paged: INC-1240 created (severity: p2).
maya: final note: after we confirm weighted tdigest merge and add the dashboard provenance, let's ship a postmortem explaining the caveat and surfacing the short-term UX/workarounds for PMs and SREs. :memo:
